Source: current agent JUnit test suite. All evaluations are deterministic and use no live LLM grading.
Reject an answer that silently selects one order when the customer did not identify it.
Concise follow-up answers only the new intent
Accept a short refund follow-up when it uses verified policy evidence and does not repeat the earlier status answer.
Reject a follow-up response containing more than 50 words.
Reject a follow-up that repeats a sequence already shown to the customer.
Lost shipment produces a grounded recommendation
Mark the shipment as an exception, report the verified lost status, and require human approval for the next action.
All tool schemas can be constructed
Create schemas successfully, including policy tools that take no arguments.
Final decision is not executed as a business tool
Treat submit_agent_decision as the final response payload instead of sending it to the tool executor.
Data tool calls reach the executor
Return ordinary data function calls so the application can execute them.
When a response also requests data tools, execute those tools before accepting a final decision.
Recognize malformed JSON or a submit_agent_decision schema failure and retry with strict structured output.
Tool loop returns a validated answer
Execute the requested tool, submit its result, validate the final decision, and report correct call counts.
Repeated invalid tool request stops safely
Stop after the same tool validation failure repeats and return SAFE_FAILURE.
Tool schema initialization failure is safe
Return SAFE_FAILURE with zero model and tool calls when the model session cannot initialize.
Accepted history is supplied to the next turn
Pass the earlier accepted customer and assistant messages into the next request and answer only the follow-up intent.
Handled safe failure has paired run events
Publish one run-started and one run-completed event with the same run ID for a handled safe failure.
Parent span is restored after a tool call
Return the logging context to the main agent span after a sequential tool call completes.
Every tool call has a unique child span
Give each tool a distinct child span and publish matching STARTED and COMPLETED events with the correct parent, trace, session, iteration, and ordinal.
List orders uses the customer-orders tool only
For a clear request to list orders, require exactly get_customer_orders before the final decision.
Identified delivery follows ownership then status
For tracking an identified order, require get_customer_orders followed by get_delivery_status.
Identified refund follows the refund path
For refund eligibility on an identified order, require ownership, delivery status, then refund policy.
Identified exchange follows the exchange path
For exchange eligibility on an identified order, require ownership, delivery status, then exchange policy.
Standalone refund policy checks orders first
For a general refund-policy question, require get_customer_orders before get_refund_policy.
Standalone exchange policy checks orders first
For a general exchange-policy question, require get_customer_orders before get_exchange_policy.
Combined policy question is not forced
Do not force a single sequence when a request combines refund and exchange intents.
Reject a proposed tool call when it does not match the next required step.
Final decision waits for the full path
Reject a final decision until every required tool in the deterministic path has completed successfully.
Agent corrects an out-of-order path before execution
Do not execute the premature tool call; send deterministic feedback, then accept the corrected ownership-to-delivery path.
After get_customer_orders returns no orders, reject get_delivery_status.
After get_customer_orders returns no orders, reject get_refund_policy.
After get_customer_orders returns no orders, reject get_exchange_policy.
Allow the final decision immediately after get_customer_orders confirms that no orders exist.
Orders-not-found error also stops the path
Treat CUSTOMER_ORDERS_NOT_FOUND as conclusive and do not call another tool.
Only fulfilled orders blocks refund policy
When every order is delivered, reject get_refund_policy as unnecessary.
Only fulfilled orders blocks exchange policy
When every order is delivered, reject get_exchange_policy as unnecessary.
An unfulfilled order keeps the refund path open
When at least one order is unfulfilled, continue to delivery status and refund policy in order.
Reject a turn that batches get_customer_orders with a later dependent tool before order results are known.
Agent executes nothing after a no-orders result
Verify the executor receives only get_customer_orders when the customer has no orders.
Agent skips refund policy for fulfilled orders
Verify get_refund_policy never reaches the executor when all customer orders are delivered.
